types.name: Scope
code: | 'tickets:read' | 'tickets:create' | 'tickets:update'   // update: title, description, fields, dates, tags, links
// PHASE 3 (§L4) — an agent that shows its work:
| 'questions:write'   // ask, cancel (and, for a person's token, answer)
| 'tasklists:write'   // publish a plan and tick it off
// ADMIN scopes — a token acting as a PERSON only; agents are never admin:
// ONE VOCABULARY FOR API KEYS, OAUTH AND MCP. can() reads ctx.scopes
// whatever door the call came through; a scope NARROWS what the
// acting principal's board role allows and never widens it:
// So a commenter agent never moves a ticket outside its StageGrant,
// PRESETS on the token form: Read only (every :read), Worker (read +
// from stored OAuth grants and older MCP clients and expanded by
// normalizeScopes(); they are never written back.

types.name: Envelope
code: id: string            // 'evt_…' — receivers dedupe on this
id: string, name: string, via: Via
via_token?: string | null    // phase 2; the token's name when a token made the change
data: T               // the public Ticket / Message shape, never the raw doc

schema.name: apiKeys
rules: allow write: never   // apiKeyCreate, apiKeyRevoke, agentArchive, boardAgentSet
// ONE BOARD PER TOKEN. Each board gets its own tokens, so a leaked
// token is one board's problem and the Tokens list reads as 'what can
// touch ENG'. A token acts as its owner, or AS ONE OF THE OWNER'S
// AGENTS that is on that board — never more than that principal's
// Shown once, stored as a hash; a lost key is rotated, not recovered.
// PHASE-1 KEYS (boardIds, no actsAs) no longer parse; the middleware
// treats them as revoked, and the Tokens list says so.
schema: boardId: BoardId        // exactly one board the owner is on
actsAs: PrincipalRef    // { kind: 'user', id: owner } | { kind: 'agent', id: agentId }
scopes: Scope[]         // agent tokens never carry board:admin / webhooks:manage
prefix: string          // 'tm_live_3fa9' — shown in the list
hash: string            // sha256 of the full key; queried by the middleware
limits: { perMin: number, perDay: number }   // default 60 / 10 000
// ACTS AS AN AGENT → the token carries the agent's identity: its changes
// are authored by the agent ('Builder (agent) via token orch-eng-builder'),
// it reads the agent's inbox and profile (system prompt included).
// The OWNER stays answerable: rate limits and idempotency key on them.
// REVOKED FOR YOU when the agent is archived (agentArchived), the agent
// is removed from the board (agentRemoved), or you leave the board
// (ownerLeft) — a token never outlives the fact it was made from.

schema.name: oauthClients
rules: allow read, write: never   // server only
schema: public: boolean         // PKCE, no secret — every MCP client
// DYNAMIC CLIENT REGISTRATION IS WHAT THE MCP AUTH SPEC EXPECTS: a
// user pastes our MCP URL into their client, the client registers
// itself, and the consent screen names it.

schema.name: oauthGrants
rules: allow delete: never   // revoke via grantRevoke, which kills the tokens too

schema.name: oauthTokens
schema: expiresAt: Millis        // access 1h, refresh 30d rotating, code 60s
// TTL policy on expiresAt deletes them; nothing sweeps by hand.

schema.name: webhooks
schema: url: string                 // https only; private IPs refused (SSRF)
failures: number            // consecutive; 20 → disabled + owner emailed

schema.name: webhookDeliveries
schema: responseSnippet: string     // first 500 bytes — for the 'Recent deliveries' panel

schema.name: installs
rules: allow write: never   // installConnect, board admin
schema: externalId: string          // GitHub installation id, Slack workspace id
repos?: { fullName: string, moveOnMerge?: string }[]   // github: repos linked to THIS board
channelId?: string; events?: WebhookEvent[]            // slack: where this board posts
// Provider tokens live in Secret Manager under integrations/{boardId}/{provider}.

schema.name: intakes
schema: // THE REFERENCE TRACKER'S 'REPORTING API', kept whole: a board made
// addressable from a website's feedback widget, authorised by a
// board-scoped slug + secret instead of a user session.
secretHash: string          // shown once, rotated — not stored in clear
limits: { perMin: 10, perHour: 100, perDay: 500 }   // the reference's defaults
fieldMap: Record<string, string>   // widget key → FieldDef.id

schema.name: deliveries
schema: inboxIds: string[]          // what this one message carried
providerId: string | null   // for status callbacks
// THE ANSWER TO 'WHY DIDN'T I GET THE EMAIL'. The reference logged
// the decision to a debug log; here it is a row the person can see

schema.name: emailThreads
schema: // replyToken = base32(ticketId + uid + HMAC) — the reply is attributed
// to the person the mail was SENT to, and only if From matches them.
messageIdHeader: string     // threading: every mail about a ticket
// replies to one phantom root (the reference's fix)

schema.name: whatsappSessions
schema: // META ONLY ALLOWS FREE-FORM MESSAGES INSIDE 24H OF THE USER'S LAST
// MESSAGE. Outside it, only approved templates — so the sender
// must know which side of the window it is on.
// Which ticket a bare reply refers to: the last one we notified about.

schema.name: rateLimits
schema: // window = floor(now / 60s) etc.; value = count via transaction()
// RTDB BECAUSE A COUNTER HERE IS ONE CHEAP TRANSACTION, not a
// contended Firestore document. Old windows deleted by housekeeping.
